name: GO Classes CS Test Series 2026 | C-Programming | Topic Wise Test 1

question.text:
Let $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ be two unknown $8$-bit $2’s$ complement numbers. We know the results of $\text{A} \;^{\wedge}\;  \text{B}$ and $\text{A} \;\&\; \text{B}$ as shown below:

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|} \hline \text{A} \;^{\wedge}\;  \text{B} & 00110100  \\\hline \text{A} \;\&\; \text{B} & 11001001 \\\hline  \end{array}$$

What is the sum $\text{A} + \text{B}$ expressed in the $8$-bit two’s complement notation?

  1. $11000110$
  2. $11000010$
  3. $01000010$
  4. $11010110$

What will be the output of the given program?

#include<stdio.h>
void main()
{
    int sum =1;
    for ( unsigned int i=3; i>=0; --i)
    {
        if(i==0) sum = sum+1;
        else sum = sum *i;
    }
    printf("%d", sum);
}
  1. $1$
  2. $7$
  3. $0$
  4. None of these

Which of the following if statement(s) below is/are equivalent to the given switch statement (that is, produces the same output under the same conditions)? Assume the answer is a previously declared int.

switch (answer)
{
    case 0: printf("0 entered"); break;
    case 1: printf("1 entered"); break;
    case 3: printf("3 entered"); break;
    case 5: printf("5 entered"); break;
    default: printf("Other value entered");
}
  1.  
    if (answer == 0 || 1 || 3 || 5)
    printf("%d entered", answer);
else
    printf("Other value entered");
  2.  
    if ((answer >= 1 && answer <= 5 && 
        answer % 2 == 1) || (answer == 0))
    printf("%d entered", answer);
else
    printf("Other value entered");
  3.  
    if (answer == 0)
    printf("0 entered");
if (answer == 1)
    printf("1 entered");
if (answer == 3)
    printf("3 entered");
if (answer == 5)
    printf("5 entered");
if (answer != 0 && answer != 1 
        && answer != 3 && answer != 5)
    printf("Other value entered");
  4.  
    if (answer == 0)
    printf("0 entered");
else if (answer == 1)
    printf("1 entered");
else if (answer == 3)
    printf("3 entered");
else if (answer == 5)
    printf("5 entered");
else if (answer != 0 & 1 & 3 & 5)
    printf("Other value entered");

What is the logical condition under which the following while loop will terminate?

int Beta = 5;
while (Beta > 0 && Beta < 10)
{
    printf("%d", Beta);
    scanf("%d", &Beta);
}
  1. Beta $<0 \;\&\&\;$ Beta $>= 10$
  2. Beta $<0 \;||$ Beta $> 10$
  3. Beta $<= 0 \;||$ Beta $>= 10$
  4. Beta $<0\; ||$ Beta $>= 10$

What will be the output of the following program?

#include<stdio.h>
main()
{
    char grade='A';
    int result=0;
    switch(grade)
    {
        case 'A':
            result+=4;
        case 'B':
            result+=3;
        case 'C':
            result+=2;
        default:
            result+=1;
    }
    printf("%d", result);
}
  1. $10$
  2. $4$
  3. $9$
  4. $0$

What will be output on the execution of the following code segment?

#include<stdio.h>
main()
{
    unsigned num1 = 1;
    signed num2 = -1;
    if (num1 < num2)
        printf("less");
    else if (num1 > num2)
        printf("greater");
    else if (num1 == num2)
        printf("equal");
}
  1. greater
  2. less
  3. equal
  4. Error

Consider two given C programs. Which of the following is/are true? It is also known that in C programming, $\&\&$ has higher precedence than $||.$

Program 1
#include<stdio.h>
void main()
{
    int i = 0;
    if (++i && (i==0))
        printf(“GO Classes\n”);
    else
        printf(“GATEOverflow\n”);
}
Program 2
#include<stdio.h>
void main()
{
    int x, y, z;
    x = 1;
    y = z = 0;
    ++x || ++y && ++z;
    if (y || z)
        printf(“GO Classes\n”);
    else
        printf(“GATEOverflow\n”);
}
  1. Program $1$ prints GO Classes
  2. Program $1$ prints GATEOverflow
  3. Program $2$ prints GO Classes
  4. Program $2$ prints GATEOverflow

What will be the output of the following C program?

#include<stdio.h>
int main(){
int x=3;
int y;
switch(x++){
    x++;
    case 3:
        printf("Three %d",x);
        break;
    case 4:
        printf("Four %d",x);
        break;
    case 5:
        printf("Five %d",x);
        break;
    default: printf("Default %d",x);
    }
}
  1. Three $3$
  2. Four $4$
  3. Three $4$
  4. Four $5$

Assume that $x$ is a two’s complement binary integer whose absolute value is not large (so no overflow problems). At right are four C expressions that use the $<<$ (shift left) and $\sim$ (bitwise complement: flip each $0$ to $1$ and each $1$ to $0$ in the binary representation) operators. For example, $7 << 1$ is $14$ and $\sim 0$ is $-1.$

Match each expression to one of the mathematical functions at left.

$$\begin{array}{|l|c|l|c|} \hline a. & 4x & \text{I.} & (\sim x) + 1 \\\hline b. & -x & \text{II.} &  (x<<1) + x \\\hline c. & 3x & \text{III.} & \sim x  \\\hline d. & -x-1 & \text{IV.} & x<<2 \\\hline \end{array}$$


  1. a - IV
    b - I
    c - II
    d - III

  2. a - IV
    b - III
    c - II
    d - I

  3. a - II
    b - I
    c - IV
    d - III
  4. None of these

Consider the $k$ bit binary pattern. $\text{T}_{\max}$ and $\text{T}_{\min}$ are maximum and minimum signed numbers we can represent using $k$ bits. $\text{U}_{\max}$ and $\text{U}_{\min}$ are maximum and minimum unsigned numbers we can represent using $k$ bits. Numbers are represented using 2's complement system.

Which of the following(s) is/are true for $k =16?$

Here $|.|$ represents absolute value of a number i.e. $|r| = -r$ if $r<0$ otherwise $|r| = r.$

  1. $|\text{T}_{\min}| = \text{T}_{\max} + 1$
  2. $\text{U}_{\max} = 2\ast \text{T}_{\max} +1$
  3. $\text{U}_{\max} = |\text{T}_{\min}| + \text{T}_{\max} + 1$
  4. $\text{U}_{\min} = |\text{T}_{\min}|$

Consider Figure A and Figure B, which represent $4$ bit signed and unsigned numbers, respectively, in the $2’s$ complement system.

Assume that a few variables are defined below and initialized in such a way that places them in the spot shown in Figure C.

int s1, s2, s3, s4;
unsigned int u1, u2, u3, u4;

Which of the following(s) is/are FALSE?

  1. $s2 > s4$
  2. $s1 > s2$
  3. $s1 > u3$
  4. $s3 > u3$

Which of the following condition(s) is/are evaluated to true for a given declaration of integer $i.$

int i = -7;
  1. $-10 < i <-1$
  2. $i \;\&\; 0 \;|\; 0\; \& \;1$
  3. $0\; \&\; 0\; \&\; 0\; |\; i$
  4. $!(1 > 0 > i \;\&\; !i)$

Consider the following program fragment. Which of the following if condition(s) prints GO Classes?

int b = 1, c = 1, d = 0;
if (0 && 0 == 0) //first if
    printf("GO Classes");
if (b || --b == 0) //Second if
    printf("GO Classes");
if (c || c-- == 0) //Third if
    printf("GO Classes");
if (d || ++d == 0) //Fourth if
    printf("GO Classes");
  1. First if condition
  2. Second if condition
  3. Third if condition
  4. Fourth if condition

The statement

while ( --counter >= 1 )
    counter % 2 ? printf("A") : printf("B");


can $\text{NOT}$ be rewritten as

  1.  
    while ( --counter >= 1 )
    if ( counter % 2 )
        printf("A");
    else
        printf("B");
  2.  
    while ( counter >= 1 )
    if (counter % 2)
        printf("A");
    else
        printf("B");
    --counter;
  3.  
    while ( counter > 1 )
{
    --counter;
    if ( counter % 2 )
        printf("A");
    else
        printf("B");
}
  4.  
    do
{
    --counter;
    printf( counter % 2 ? "A" : "B" );
} while ( counter >= 2 );

Imagine that our system uses a $5$-bit integer representation and does addition and subtraction using the rules for $5$-bit, two’s complement arithmetic.

Which of the following is/are TRUE?

When converting to decimal, you should treat the value as either signed or unsigned according to the rules of C, where $\text{T}_{\min}$ and $\text{T}_{\max}$ are signed, as are plain constants, but a constant ending in $\text{U}$ is unsigned.

  1. $\text{-T}_{\max} - 1\text{U}$ is $16$ in decimal
  2. $\text{-T}_{\max} - \text{T}_{\min}$ is $00001$ in binary
  3. $\text{T}_{\max} + \text{T}_{\max}$ is $-2$ in decimal
  4. $\text{T}_{\min} - 1\text{U}$ is $15$ in decimal
